user:
Project: React. Upgrade being assessed: 17 -> 18.
This change was introduced in release 18. Source: How to Upgrade to React 18 (official_migration_guide). Section: Updates to TypeScript definitions.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
If your project uses TypeScript, you will need to update your @types/react and @types/react-dom dependencies to the latest versions. The new types are safer and catch issues that used to be ignored by the type checker. The most notable change is that the children prop now needs to be listed explicitly when defining props, for example: interface MyButtonProps { color: string; children?: React.ReactNode; }
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
Updates to TypeScript definitions: If your project uses TypeScript, you will need to update your @types/react and @types/react-dom dependencies to the latest versions. The new types are safer and catch issues that used to be ignored by the type checker. The most notable change is that the children prop now needs to be listed explicitly when defining props, for example: interface MyButtonProps { color: string; children?: React.ReactNode; } See the React 18 typings pull request for a full list of type-only changes. It links to example fixes in library types so you can see how to adjust your code. You can use the automated migration script to help port your application code to the new and safer typings faster. If you find a bug in the typings, please file an issue in the DefinitelyTyped repo.
>>>

Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 18 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 18 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. Use derived_by "inference" for any condition not directly stated.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.path_name: TypeScript children prop must be declared explicitly in props types

conditions.statement: The upgrade crosses React 18, which ships the new, stricter TypeScript definitions.
quotes: The most notable change is that the children prop now needs to be listed explicitly when defining props
conditions.relevance: Ties the typing change to the React 18 upgrade.

conditions.statement: The project uses TypeScript and depends on @types/react and @types/react-dom, which must be updated to the latest versions.
quotes: If your project uses TypeScript, you will need to update your @types/react and @types/react-dom dependencies to the latest versions.
conditions.relevance: The new typings are delivered via these packages; TypeScript projects need to update them.
ambiguities: The text does not give a specific minimum version of @types/react or @types/react-dom.

conditions.statement: Component props types (interfaces/types) rely on implicit children without declaring a children prop, which the new types now flag as type errors.
conditions.expected_value: children?: React.ReactNode in props types of components that accept children
quotes: The new types are safer and catch issues that used to be ignored by the type checker.
interface MyButtonProps { color: string; children?: React.ReactNode; }
conditions.relevance: Components whose props do not list children but are given children will fail type checking after updating types.
ambiguities: The text does not explicitly state that the type check fails; this is inferred from the change that children must be listed explicitly.

suggested_actions: Update @types/react and @types/react-dom to the latest versions.
Add children?: React.ReactNode explicitly to props interfaces/types of components that accept children.
Use the automated migration script mentioned in the guide to port application code to the new typings.
See the React 18 typings pull request for the full list of type-only changes.
